text:
CF clinic review

31F with cystic fibrosis, F508del homozygous, followed here since transition from paediatrics.

Two exacerbations this year, both treated at home with oral ciprofloxacin. FEV1 today 1.62 L,
54% predicted, down from 61% in March.

Sputum grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa in September and eradication was completed in October.

CF related diabetes diagnosed in 2009, on insulin, HbA1c 7.8% last month.

She has not had a pneumothorax and has never needed non-invasive ventilation.

Mother has coeliac disease. No family history of lung disease other than her own.

Plan: annual review bloods, DEXA due, refer to the transplant assessment clinic if the FEV1
falls below 40% predicted.

Renal clinic

Referred with a rising creatinine on the CF annual bloods.

Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL today, was 0.9 mg/dL eighteen months ago. eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73m2. Urine ACR
12 mg/mmol.

Long history of aminoglycoside exposure for CF exacerbations, plus CF related diabetes since
2009. Both are plausible contributors.

Renal ultrasound: kidneys 10.4 and 10.1 cm, normal cortical thickness, no obstruction, a simple
2 cm cyst on the right.

Mesenteric ischaemia was excluded on the CT angiogram done in November for her abdominal pain,
so the abdominal symptoms are not vascular.

Diabetic nephropathy is the working diagnosis but no biopsy has been done and I would not push
for one.

Repeat bloods 3/12. Avoid NSAIDs. Copy to the CF team.

Phone call from patient, 14:20.

Increased sputum volume over 4 days, now green. No haemoptysis. Breathless on the stairs, which
is new for her. Temp 37.8 at home.

Appetite poor. Weight down 1.2 kg since clinic.

Sats 94% on the home oximeter.

Discussed with the on call CF consultant. To come in this afternoon for IV antibiotics via the
port.

Reminded her to call 999 rather than wait for the morning if she deteriorates overnight.
